summary: Nimbus Freight dedicated: sudden in-flight request-count surge after DST change causing duplicate completions and billing spike
description: Issue summary: Between 2026-03-10 11:50-12:55 UTC Nimbus Freight reported a rapid increase in in-flight request counts and duplicate completions. Customer observed increased token billing (3x baseline) and duplicated responses for ~35% of requests. Impact: customer-facing endpoints for fulfillment chat and webhook completions experienced elevated latencies and duplicated responses causing downstream reconciliation failures and invoice exposure. Environment: Dedicated GPU pool (nimbus-dedicated-01), prod-us-east, autoscale enabled, custom retry middleware at customer side. Immediate symptoms: spike in inflight metrics, autoscaler repeatedly adding capacity then quickly shedding, many requests retried at client causing duplicated completions. This ticket covers investigation, mitigation, root cause, and post-incident action items.
timeline: 2026-03-10T11:46Z - Nimbus alert: elevated token usage; 11:50 - Support received first customer message; 11:55 - Observed inflight counter rising from 1200->4300 across pool; 12:02 - Stream duplicates confirmed by replay; 12:10 - Canary fallback configured to route to warm backup pool; 12:25 - Autoscaler policy adjusted to increase min nodes and hold scale for 10m; 12:55 - Duplicate completions rate dropped below 1%; 13:30 - Billing mitigation credit issued; 2026-03-12 - Root cause patch deployed to scheduler and customer-facing middleware recommendations published.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use dedicated capacity with autoscaler configured for rapid scale-up/scale-down and client retry middleware with timeout 8s. 2) Simulate clock shift: system toggles DST-affecting timestamp in orchestration control plane (advance local scheduling epoch by 1 hour). 3) Send steady 800 RPS workload with varied prompt lengths. 4) Observe inflight counters double-counting (scheduler reports duplicates), autoscaler thrash, and clients with retry logic receive duplicate completions when requests are reissued during transient scheduling mismatch.

investigation_notes: Hypotheses evaluated: 1) noisy neighbor - low signal. 2) model kernel regression - not correlated with model change. 3) control-plane epoch/timestamp drift after a DST/time-sync event - strong correlation. Findings: an internal maintenance job that adjusts scheduling epochs for internal metrics executed a cron job intended for a different timezone and applied a +3600s drift to the scheduler's epoch bucket for nimbus-dedicated-01. The scheduler's inflight accounting uses epoch-based lease ids; when the epoch shifted mid-flight some inflight leases were double-acknowledged by worker nodes leading to double-counting and premature ACKs that allowed client retries to re-enter the system. The autoscaler reacted to inflated metrics causing capacity thrash; duplicated processing occurred for requests that were retried by the customer within the retry window. Cross-reference: Slack thread #support-nimbus (https://slack.redwood.ai/support-nimbus/p12345), PR fixing epoch drift handling (github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/4217).
mitigation: Short-term: 1) Applied emergency config to freeze epoch updates on dedicated pools (11:58). 2) Increased autoscaler stabilization window and bumped min_nodes to prevent thrash (12:25). 3) Configured temporary dedupe filter at api-gateway for requests with identical client-provided id for 1 hour (12:30). 4) Issued billing credit covering estimated overage while investigation ongoing (12:40). Long-term: deploy scheduler patch to ignore unintended epoch deltas and add validation, add stronger prechecks for cron timezone context, and publish recommended client-side idempotency guidance.
resolution: Root cause: scheduler epoch drift caused by maintenance job applying a timezone-shifted epoch to the scheduler control-plane for dedicated pool nimbus-dedicated-01. Fix: merged scheduler patch that validates epoch deltas and enforces monotonic leases (merged PR #4217 and deployed 2026-03-12 02:10 UTC). Added api-gateway dedupe as safety net. Customer outcome: duplicate completions reduced to <0.5%, autoscaler stabilized, and billing credit issued for anomalous token consumption (credited on 2026-03-11 invoice). Ticket status moved to Resolved after verification period and customer acceptance.
action_items: 1) Scheduler: add epoch delta safety guard and integration test for DST/timezone edgecases - owner @infra-scheduler, due 2026-03-17
2) Runbook: create 'epoch drift' playbook and checklist for maintenance jobs - owner @sre, due 2026-03-16
3) Autoscaler: add hysteresis and backoff when inflight counters change >30% in 2m - owner @autoscaler-team, due 2026-03-19
4) Docs/SDK: publish idempotency header guidance and recommend client-generated request_id best practices - owner @developer-experience, due 2026-03-18
5) Billing: finalize credit calculation and confirm invoice adjustment with customer - owner @finance, due 2026-03-13
